case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses Bluetooth SIG qualification strategy for a TV product undergoing only an OS version upgrade without RF hardware changes. The customer wanted to reuse existing RF/RF PHY test reports from a prior qualification listing to avoid unnecessary retesting. The consultant analyzed the existing Controller Subsystem selection and identified qualification database inconsistencies and new rule impacts introduced after July 1, 2024. The discussion evolved into a strategy recommendation using a compatible Subset QDID and inherited profile qualifications to avoid large-scale retesting and future IOPT obligations. The thread also addressed the impact of QPRDv4 IOPT requirements becoming effective on November 10, 2025.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical discussion focused on whether prior RF/RF PHY reports could be reused when there was no wireless module or RF specification change. During analysis, the consultant found that the proposed Controller Subsystem registration had RF/RF PHY and LL ICS differences versus the historical listing, including Power Class differences. Attempting to resolve the mismatch through ICS modification would trigger approximately 300 LL test report upload requirements under the post-July-2024 SIG registration process and expose existing hierarchy inconsistencies in the referenced Controller Subsystem. The consultant instead proposed using a compatible Subset registration with matching RF/RF PHY characteristics that avoided hierarchy inconsistencies. The thread also explained that inheriting A2DP and other profile qualifications from an earlier QDID at the ICS level could eliminate profile testing and report upload requirements if no new profile functionality had been added.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's core reasoning was to minimize qualification scope changes so the project could remain inside previously qualified RF, RF PHY, and profile boundaries. Because the proposed Controller Subsystem created LL ICS inconsistencies and triggered extensive new test requirements under newer SIG policies, the correct approach was to select a compatible Subset QDID with matching RF/RF PHY behavior and no hierarchy inconsistency. The consultant also determined that profile testing could be avoided if the FY26 implementation exactly matched the profile ICS capabilities already qualified in the FY23 QDID. Finally, the consultant recognized that registration timing relative to the QPRDv4 IOPT effective date directly determined whether additional mandatory testing would apply.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using the incompatible Controller Subsystem registration or modifying LL ICS incorrectly could trigger approximately 300 additional LL-related test evidence uploads and create unrealistic testing cost and schedule impact. Incorrect subsystem selection could also create cascading hierarchy inconsistency issues that generate additional qualification requirements. If profile inheritance were attempted despite added functionality, the qualification could become invalid or incomplete. Delaying registration beyond the QPRDv4 IOPT effective date would additionally introduce mandatory IOPT profile testing and associated extra cost.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When handling Bluetooth SIG re-listings for OS-only updates, consultants should aggressively preserve reuse eligibility by matching RF/RF PHY behavior, avoiding unnecessary ICS changes, selecting compatible subset QDIDs, and inheriting prior profile qualifications whenever implementation scope has not changed. Registration timing against evolving QPRD policy effective dates can materially affect required testing scope and project cost.
